_description: Phase 4.5: every rule in validate-calculator-content.mjs, existing and newly added, with purpose/severity/false-positive testing against the 13 shipped files (instruction 36).

existingRules.purpose: Prevents scope creep (content for an unapproved calculator) or silent gaps (a missing one).
Same class of bug Phase 2 found in catalog names.
Content and SEO map can't silently disagree on depth.
existingRules.testedAgainst13: 0 hits (after the test-duration-estimator depth-model fix, which didn't touch any of the 13)

existingRules.purpose: Flags when a page is missing content a depth-appropriate page should have.
existingRules.falsePositiveRisk: medium before this audit - the mapping over-credited 'formula' sections for workedExample without checking the example was actually present. Fixed by rule 'worked-example-presence' below.
existingRules.testedAgainst13: 0 hits after all Phase 4 gaps were fixed
existingRules.status: kept, backed by the new mechanical check

existingRules.purpose: A light page shouldn't carry a methodology/assumptions/limitations section it doesn't need.

existingRules.rule: duplicate section ids / duplicate FAQ questions

existingRules.purpose: Catches unfinished drafts shipped by accident.
Two pages can't compete for the exact same SERP snippet.
Catches introductions that read as copies of each other.
existingRules.falsePositiveRisk: low - Jaccard on 4+ letter words is a blunt instrument, but 0.35 is a high enough bar that it hasn't false-positived on genuinely-different-but-topically-related intros (e.g. cac/cac-payback-period, which share vocabulary but scored well under 0.35).

medium - structural sameness isn't the same as prose sameness (instruction 5's own point). Two sequences hit 3-4 pages each, below the 5-page trigger, so this rule hasn't actually fired yet even though the audit found real (and judged acceptable) repetition via the new heading-level check instead.
existingRules.status: unchanged - kept as a second, coarser signal alongside the new heading-level check

newRulesAddedThisPhase.what_it_detects: For any calculator whose slot template requires workedExample, checks that at least one number from the calculator's own exampleInput/exampleOutput (or examplesByMode) literally appears in a formula/example/models section's text - not just that a section with the right `type` exists.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.why_it_matters: This was the single biggest scaling risk found in the audit (Section 1): the old TYPE_TO_SLOTS credit assumed every 'formula' section embeds a real example because that happened to be true for all 12 shipped ones, with nothing actually verifying it. At 40+ pages, a future formula section that skips the example would pass silently.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.severity: warning (not error - a page can legitimately explain 'why' without repeating the exact example numbers a second time in a different section, so this flags for review rather than blocking)
newRulesAddedThisPhase.falsePositiveRisk: low for flat scalar-input calculators (all 13 shipped ones); intentionally skipped for array-input calculators (funnel-analysis-multistep and future ones) where the exampleInput isn't a flat key/value pair the number-matching can reliably parse against prose - documented in the code comment, not silently wrong.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.testedAgainst13: 0 warnings - confirms every shipped page's example claim is backed by the actual number, not just asserted

newRulesAddedThisPhase.what_it_detects: 17 known AI-filler phrases (instruction 15's list plus a few observed in the wild: 'leverage', 'robust', 'seamless', 'game-changing') anywhere in intro/section/model prose.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.why_it_matters: The single most direct check against the content reading as machine-generated at scale, and the cheapest one to run - pure string matching.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.falsePositiveRisk: some patterns (e.g. 'robust') can appear in genuinely relevant technical prose (e.g. 'a robust standard error estimate') - deliberately kept as a warning, never an error, per instruction 15.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.testedAgainst13: 0 hits - matches the manual grep run earlier in this audit

newRulesAddedThisPhase.what_it_detects: The exact same section heading string used on 4 or more content files.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.why_it_matters: Directly surfaced the audit's own finding: 'Reading the number' on 8/13 pages, 'The formula' on 5/13. Makes this visible automatically as the corpus grows instead of requiring another manual grep.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.severity: warning, explicitly excluding 'Common mistakes' (a utility label expected to repeat, not a claim)
newRulesAddedThisPhase.falsePositiveRisk: by design this rule doesn't distinguish healthy consistency from real template risk - that judgment call is documented in this audit (calculator-content-system-audit.md), not automated. The warning message says so explicitly so a future reviewer doesn't have to re-litigate it from scratch.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.testedAgainst13: 2 hits, both real and already reviewed as healthy (see calculator-content-system-audit.md)

newRulesAddedThisPhase.what_it_detects: Two different calculators' primaryKeyword strings (Phase 3's calculator-seo-map.json) that substring-overlap after normalization, with neither a Phase 3 cannibalizationRisk flag nor a comparison-note on either page.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.why_it_matters: Backstops Phase 3's cannibalizationRisks list, which came from the brief's named examples (10 pairs), not an exhaustive pairwise scan across all 77 - a real future collision could exist that Phase 3 never looked at.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.falsePositiveRisk: medium - a >4-character substring match is a blunt signal (e.g. two calculators both containing the word 'rate' at the right length could theoretically trip it). Tuned to require >4 characters specifically to avoid 3-letter acronym false positives (cac/cac-payback-period didn't fire); should be revisited if it gets noisy once the 21 live-but-unwritten calculators get content.

newRulesAddedThisPhase.rule: benchmark section requires a resolvable sourceId
newRulesAddedThisPhase.what_it_detects: Any section typed 'benchmark' must carry a `benchmark.sourceId` that exists in calculator-content-sources.json.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.why_it_matters: Structurally enforces the benchmark policy (instruction 8) instead of relying on editorial discipline alone - the schema change (calculator-content.schema.json) makes 'benchmark' its own type distinct from 'interpretation', and this validator rule makes it impossible to ship a sourceless benchmark claim without the build failing.
newRulesAddedThisPhase.testedAgainst13: 0 hits (no page uses the benchmark type yet - none met the sourcing bar, see calculator-content-sources.json)
